oc-flight-deck

Live cost, token, cache and context telemetry for every OpenCode session, drawn in your sidebar.

## Why Cost and context are easy to lose sight of during a long session. `oc-flight-deck` draws them beside the session, live, so you see the roll-up without leaving the run. A cache hit rate excludes writes from its denominator, because a write is not a lookup. Elapsed time is recomputed from the turn spans the host recorded, so it survives a restart and never steps backwards. Estimates carry a `~` and say so out loud. Every setting lives in one global file, not per project. ## Install Add the entry to the `plugins` array in your `opencode.jsonc`, then restart OpenCode: ```json { "plugins": ["oc-flight-deck"] } ``` ## Use The rail draws up to 18 named rows in the order you choose. Among them are: - **Honest zeros** — every numeric row draws a real zero when there is no data, never a dash or a blank. - **Money** — the current model's spend for this session, and a durable lifetime total for the subagent tree. The old `cost` and `total` row names still work as aliases. - **Tokens and cache** — input and output tokens, and a cache hit rate with writes excluded. - **Context gauge** — occupancy as a bar plus a percentage, marked `~` when estimated. - **Speed** — a settled-turn average, a realtime estimate, or both plus time to first token. - **Caution annunciator** — an opt-in watchdog that stays silent until a tool or a turn stops moving, and reports what it saw without killing anything. - **Quota and session rows** — the Go usage dials, and a session id row that copies the full id on click. ## Configure All settings live in one global file; there are no per-project files. Start from the [example config](https://github.com/nathwn12/oc-collections/blob/main/packages/oc-flight-deck/flight-deck.example.jsonc) and check the [schema](https://github.com/nathwn12/oc-collections/blob/main/packages/oc-flight-deck/flight-deck.schema.json) for each key and its default. ## Requirements - OpenCode 2.1.1 or newer. - Node 22 or newer, or Bun 1.4 or newer. - Any platform the host runs on. ## Links - [Issues](https://github.com/nathwn12/oc-collections/issues) - [Releases](https://github.com/nathwn12/oc-collections/releases) - [Guide](https://github.com/nathwn12/oc-collections/blob/main/packages/oc-flight-deck/docs/GUIDE.md) - [MIT licence](https://github.com/nathwn12/oc-collections/blob/main/LICENSE)

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.25.1] - 2026-11-20

### Fixed

- The `caution` row no longer reports `no progress` for an idle session: silent-turn now needs an open turn, not just a stale host `running` flag. The `status` row reads idle on stale running, paused when a permission or a question tool waits, and running only with real evidence.

### Added

- Clearer row names `spend` and `lifetime` are now the defaults. `cost` and `total` remain accepted aliases with their old labels and meaning; naming both an alias and its key renders once and reports the duplicate.
- The `total` row is now a durable high-water mark: the highest family figure seen for a session root is kept under `~/.local/share/opencode/flight-deck/totals.json`, so restarts and host pruning cannot lower it. The current-model spend row is unchanged.

### Changed

- Every numeric sidebar row now draws an honest zero instead of hiding or drawing a placeholder. The `tps` row sticks at `0 <label>` when nothing generates; observed TTFT rides only while a rate stands. The default `sidebar.placeholder` is now `0` for the text rows that still need one.

## [0.24.0] - 2026-11-17

### Added

- Opt-in `dex` sidebar row: compact 5h and 1w Codex account dials match the Go row. Windows uses a private authenticated stdio server enclosed in an owned Job Object; no shared daemon, OAuth credential-file access or process-tree kills.

### Changed

- The TPS row defaults to the realtime estimate and includes observed time to first token when available. The settled-turn average remains opt-in.
- Missing TPS uses the configured placeholder instead of a misleading zero; observed TTFT remains visible between streams.

### Fixed

- The compact Go row shows reset countdowns with the same two-unit precision as the Go panel instead of rounding hours or days up to a single unit.

## [0.22.0] - 2026-11-10

### Changed

- The plugin ids now carry the package name: the server entry is `oc-flight-deck.host` (was `flight-deck.host`) and the TUI entry is `oc-flight-deck` (was `flight-deck-tui`). A plugin inventory that labels a server entry by its id with the `.host` suffix stripped now reads `oc-flight-deck`.

### Migration

- A directive keyed by the old id stops matching: an enable/disable record for `flight-deck-tui` or `flight-deck.host` must be re-pointed at the new id.
- Everything else survives untouched: the persisted state keys `flight-deck.guard`, `flight-deck.go` and `flight-deck.frame`, and the config path `~/.config/opencode/flight-deck.jsonc`.

## [0.21.1] - 2026-11-01

### Fixed

- `@opencode/plugin` is a runtime dependency; as an optional peer it was absent from the published install, so both entrypoints threw ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

## [0.21.0] - 2026-10-31

### Changed

- The `@opencode/plugin` development pin is `2.2.4`, exact rather than a caret or `latest`: the fixture requires a concrete version, and the types and the build read exactly one SDK. No source change and no peer-range change: `@opencode/plugin` stays `>=2.1.1 <3`.

### Breaking, relative to 0.20.7

- `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` peer ranges are `>=0.8.0`, up from `>=0.6.6`. A host below 0.8.0 is outside the declared range.

## [0.20.7] - 2026-10-30

### Changed

- `cost` and `total` no longer prefix an estimated figure with `~`. An estimated figure is still catalog-priced rather than a recorded charge; only its mark is gone, because the mark cost more width than the distinction earned. The `≥` floor mark stays: it says the figure counts only the history the host still holds.

## [0.20.6] - 2026-10-29

### Changed

- Dependency pins move to the host's current line: `@opencode/plugin` 2.2.0 → 2.2.1 for types and build, and the `@opentui/core` / `@opentui/solid` dev pins 0.6.6 → 0.7.0 to match the renderer the host ships. No source change and no peer-range change: `@opencode/plugin` stays `>=2.1.1 <3` and `@opentui/core` / `@opentui/solid` stay `>=0.6.6`, so a host on the 2.1.x line or on the 0.6.x renderer still loads the same build. `@opencode/theme` is not declared by this package.

## [0.20.5] - 2026-10-28

### Added

- Opt-in `updated` row: the absolute timestamp of the newest action the host recorded for the session — the latest message's `completed`, else `streamed`, else `created` stamp. Off the shipped rail, like `branch` and `go`: add `"updated"` to `sidebar.rows` to draw it. `format.timestamp` sets the presentation: `locale` (default the host locale), `dateStyle` (`"short"` default, `"medium"`, or `"none"`), `timeStyle` (`"medium"` default with seconds, `"short"`, or `"none"`), `hour12` (omit to follow the locale, or force 12/24-hour), and `timeZone` (omit for the host zone, or name an IANA zone or UTC offset). Omitted `timeZone` leaves Intl's own host-zone default in place, so no Windows-to-IANA table ships here; a Windows zone id or an unknown name is reported and falls back to the host zone without breaking the rail. A config that turns both style halves `"none"` is reported and restored to the defaults. With `sidebar.persist` the row draws `sidebar.placeholder` until the host records an action, since there is no honest zero timestamp.

### Fixed

- `cost` and `total` now read the host's own figures. `total` is the family roll-up (`data.session.cost(root(sessionID))`), resolved from the session's root because `cost()` answers a family only for a root. It is drawn as exact only when the host's family records are complete and consistent with the charges visible on the message lists - every listed member on record, and a roll-up that already covers them. Otherwise the host's figure is shown as a floor (`>=`) and is never raised above itself; when the host reports zero, the visible recorded sum is shown as a floor; `$0.000` is exact only for a complete family with nothing recorded or visible, and incomplete coverage with nothing visible is a floor at zero. a zero roll-up where the family still holds tokens on models the catalog prices is a catalog estimate across the whole family, marked `~`, never exact. `cost` is the current model's spend: the recorded cost of the assistant steps that ran on the selected model, excluding anything older than the session's own creation (the host's own fork guard, so copied parent history is not billed to the fork), and marked as a floor because the TUI surface exposes a window of history with no paging. A step whose charge was not recorded is catalog-priced and marked `~`. The session aggregate is never used as a per-model figure, and no price table ships in this package. `@opencode/plugin` moves to 2.2.0 for types.
- The rail's count formatter now steps past millions: a 1,769,100,000 cache read draws as `1.8B` instead of `1769.1M`, and the 999,950,000 boundary draws as `1B` instead of `1000M`. The `B` and `T` steps carry the same one-decimal shape as `M`, and the round-before-unit rule holds at every boundary up to the deliberate `T` ceiling (a token count at ~999.95T would still read `1000T`).

## [0.20.4] - 2026-10-23

- Pipeline-verification patch; no functional change.

## [0.20.3] - 2026-10-23

- `@opencode/plugin` is no longer a runtime dependency. It moves to an optional peer range (`>=2.1.1 <3`), with 2.1.3 as a dev dependency for types, so an install no longer carries its own copy of the host module.
- Rationale: the host serves `@opencode/plugin` and its subpaths from its own package tree at load time and refuses a copy loaded from a plugin's `node_modules`, so the bundled copy was never used - it only added a duplicate install tree (a clean `npm install @opencode/plugin@2.1.3` measures 127 MB across 167 packages) beside every plugin.
- No behaviour change; hosts on 2.1.1 and 2.1.3 are both supported.

## [0.20.2] - 2026-10-22

- Version bump for the monorepo release; no runtime change.
- npm is the only documented install route; the git and local-clone routes were removed from the docs.

## [0.20.1] - 2026-10-21

### Changed

- Host SDK `@opencode/plugin` 2.0.30 → 2.1.1; opentui peers `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` 0.5.17 → 0.6.6 (`peerDependencies >=0.6.6`).
- No behaviour change: `src/` has no use of the removed `session.compacted` event or the renamed provider replay fields (`providerState`, `providerResultState`, `resultState`, `providerContext`), so nothing else moved.

## [0.20.0] - 2026-10-17

### Added

- `notifications` section (`enabled`, `config`, `copy`, `caution`, all default `true`): the silencing layer over every toast the plugin can raise — the invalid-config warning, the copy outcome, and the opt-in caution toast. `"notifications": { "enabled": false }` is the one-line silence switch; each per-kind flag silences only its kind. `caution.toast` stays the feature opt-in (default `false`); the new section only ever silences, never enables.

- `sidebar.tps.display` (`"avg"`, `"rt"` or `"both"`, default `"avg"`): which figure the `tps` row draws. `avg` is the settled-turn average — generation tokens (output plus reasoning) over assistant turns that recorded `streamed`, divided by the union of their `streamed − created` spans — so an idle gap reads as a steady figure instead of zero and in-flight turns never dilute it (on hosts without turn timestamps the average is generation tokens over the borrowed active clock instead). `rt` is the realtime estimate from the host's streaming delta events (`session.text.delta` / `session.reasoning.delta`, tokens estimated from delta bytes because the host publishes real counts only at step end), reading zero while nothing generates. `both` draws both on one line (`106 rt · 41 avg`), degrading to the realtime half alone when nothing settled yet. An unknown value falls back to `"avg"` and is reported.

- Mean time to first token on the `both` line (`83 rt · 38 avg · 1.2s ttft`): the mean over the most recent finalized steps in the row's scope — per step, the earliest text/reasoning delta's event time minus the step's `started` dispatch stamp (request dispatch time, before waiting for provider output), pushed into the scope's ring when the step ends. Steps observed while the plugin ran only (in-memory; a restart forgets them), so eviction drops whole values and the mean can never be negative or fabricated. A step's TTFT appears once that step settles. Appended only once a finalized value exists; the line is unchanged until then and the single modes never draw it.

### Changed

- The `tps` row now defaults to the settled-turn average (`sidebar.tps.display: "avg"`) instead of the realtime figure: the row holds steady through idle gaps between turns and draws on the first poll with nothing to estimate. `rt` drives the realtime figure from the host's streaming delta events (`session.text.delta` / `session.reasoning.delta`, estimating tokens from delta bytes) instead of the previous per-poll message scan — which could only see a turn's tokens after it settled, so it read 0 until the turn was done. An in-flight message carries no streaming text and no token counts; the realtime figure must come from the deltas. The `display: "live"` name is renamed to `"rt"` (no alias; an unknown value falls back to `"avg"`), a plain wording change — the option was never tagged, so no version bump.

### Fixed

- The session-id copy is now really verified: the plugin uses the host-served clipboard (`createHostClipboard` from `@opentui/core`, resolved to the host's own core instance) instead of no backend, and an OSC52 dispatch is confirmed by reading the OS clipboard back (up to 5 attempts, 60ms apart) before it counts — `osc52-confirmed` stays silent like every verified copy, while an unconfirmed dispatch keeps its advisory warning.
- The `0.19.2` tag shipped a stale `dist/`: `src/tui/clipboard.ts` changed without a rebuild, so installs still showed the old toast. `dist/` is rebuilt in this commit, and the new `bun run check:dist` gate (wired into `check.yml`) fails when `dist/` drifts from source again.
- The `ses` row's unconfirmed OSC52 dispatch reports as an advisory `warning` ("paste to verify") instead of an error: the bytes were sent but no backend can confirm the terminal acted on them. The five genuine failures stay `error`, and only a verified copy ever reports success.

## [0.19.2] - 2026-10-16

### Fixed

- The README and INSTALL no longer claim the package is unpublished: the `0.19.1` tarball shipped that stale text (corrected in docs after the tag), so this release ships the corrected wording.

## [0.19.1] - 2026-10-16

### Changed

- The TUI entrypoint now consumes the host renderer instead of shipping its own `@opentui/*` copy: `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` moved from `dependencies` to `peerDependencies`-only (`>=0.5.17`, matching the host), per the official CLI plugin contract. Opencode v2.0.30 refuses to load a plugin that ships and value-imports its own `@opentui/core`, so the vendored value imports are gone: the OSC52 fallback calls the host renderer's `copyToClipboardOSC52` structurally (same capability gating as before), and the text-attribute bits are pinned as local literals asserted against the vendored enum in tests. There is no sanctioned host clipboard surface, so without a renderer fallback the copy path reports `no-backend` instead of throwing. `@opencode/plugin` is pinned to the current host version `2.0.30`.

### Added

- `layout.labels`: rename any rail row's label, keyed by the row name exactly as `sidebar.rows` spells it (`session` is folded to `ses`). `{ "cost": "session", "total": "lifetime" }` draws the session's own cost under `session` and the family total under `lifetime`; every row left out keeps its built-in label, so an install that never sets the key renders byte-identically to before. An unknown row name, a non-string value, or an empty label is reported as a config issue naming its path (`layout.labels.<name>`) and that row falls back to its default label. Both renderers resolve a row's label from the same map, so the plain-string view and the segmented (`style.rows`) view never disagree.
- `sidebar.tps.scope` (`"family"` or `"session"`, default `"family"`): which sessions the `tps` row paces. `family` sums generation tokens (output plus reasoning) across the open session and its subagent sessions over the union of all their streaming spans — concurrent decoders share wall clock, so overlapping spans merge instead of adding, and a root that is idle while its child decodes still reads live. `session` restores the previous per-session figure: the open session's own tokens over its own spans. An unknown value falls back to `"family"` and is reported.

### Changed

- The `total` row draws the real family figure for a childless session: its own cost with `0 subagents`, instead of the persist layer's live-shaped `$0.000`. `treeTotals` now records a family of one as the session's own cost against a count of zero rather than returning nothing, and the row renders whenever a family figure exists — so a session that spawned no subagents still reads its lifetime figure under that row. `total` stays absent, and the unchanged skeleton draws, only when there is genuinely no tree or cost data at all (a session with no record yet), and a child session still has no `total` of its own. A session with subagents sums them exactly as before.

### Fixed

- Opencode 2.0.30 compatibility: the shipped entries are now plain compiled JS in `dist/` (`bun run compile`), not raw source. A raw `.tsx` entry under `node_modules` falls back to Bun's native JSX transform on this host, whose injected `jsx-dev-runtime` import bypasses the rewrite loader and fails to resolve — so the TUI entry ships with explicit `jsx`/`jsxs` imports from `@opentui/solid/jsx-runtime` and no raw JSX. `package.json` `exports` (`"."` and `"./tui"`) and `files` point at `dist/` (`src` stays for types and dev), `@opentui/*` and `solid-js`/`solid-js/store` stay external with nothing bundled or copied.

## [0.19.0] - 2026-10-11

### Added

- `session` is accepted as an alias for the `ses` row in `sidebar.rows` and `style.rows`, normalized to `ses`. The row's rail label is now `session`: an 18-cell clipped preview of the id (never the full id), with the click still copying the full id to the terminal clipboard. The preview budget shrinks by however much the `session` label overflows `layout.labelWidth`, floored at 8 cells, so the row's total width is unchanged by the rename at every `layout.labelWidth` (at the default width 10 the budget is the full 18; at 6 it is 17).
- Zero skeletons for data-less rows under `sidebar.persist`: a row with no data draws a real-looking zero instead of the `—` placeholder — `$0.000` for `cost`/`total`/`project`, `0 in · 0 out` for `tokens`, `0 read` for `cache`, an empty bar plus `~0%` for `context`, `0 waiting` for `perms`, `0s` for `elapsed`, `0 tok/s` for `tps`, a flat `▁` bar for `spark`, `0` for `reasoning`, `0` for `turns`, `○ 0 ○ 0 ○ 0` for `go`, `○ idle` for `status`, `none` for `agent`/`model`/`ses`, `no branch` for `branch`, `unknown` for `guard`. `caution` is the one row that never draws a skeleton: the annunciator stays silent until there is something to announce. `sidebar.placeholder` is now only the fallback for a field with no skeleton, so the dash is unreachable in practice.

### Changed

- `tokens`, `cache` and `reasoning` read the same family scope as `cost`: this conversation plus its subagent sessions when any exist, the session alone when there are none.
- `elapsed` is recomputed from the assistant-turn spans the host itself recorded for this session and its subagents, a turn still in flight ending at "now". A restart comes back with the same value instead of resetting, it cannot step backwards while the host still reports those turns, it freezes the instant everything settles, and it is NOT wall-clock since the session began.
- `tps` is directly per-session — subagents excluded: the displayed session's own generation tokens (output + reasoning) over its own generating time. It shows `0 tok/s` whenever the session is not generating (idle, between turns, or before the first sample), and it never seeds itself from a lifetime average.
- The `cost` row documents its limit plainly: the rollup follows the host's `parentID` link only (`family()`), so a session spawned as an independent top-level session — a `commander` spawning captains — carries no `parentID`, and the host returned no `metadata` field for the sessions probed during this work, so there is no automatic creator link today. A creator-supplied attribution link is a possible future extension, not a shipped feature. The `project` row is the surface that covers every session in the project, spawned sessions included.

### Fixed

- The `tps` row no longer claims subagents are included: the figure never covered them, and the docs said it did.

## [0.17.0] - 2026-10-10

### Added

- `sidebar.footer.go` accepts `align` (`left`, `right`, `center`, default `right`): where each trailing value sits inside its own fixed-width percent (4) and reset (6) cell. `right` pins the value to the cell's right edge, so the digits stay put as values change length; `left` hugs the bar with the padding trailing; `center` splits the padding. Both trailing cells use the same setting, and the cell widths never move.

### Removed

- The `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` environment fallback is gone: the `go` row and the footer Go panel resolve the Zen Go key only from OpenCode's own credential sources (the credential store, then the provider catalog's resolved `settings.apiKey`). With no usable entry the bridge stores null and reports the `no-key` reason without making a request.

## [0.15.0] - 2026-10-11

### Changed

- The footer Go panel draws three strict fixed-width columns - label (6, `ROLL`/`WEEK`/`MONTH`), meter (14), right-aligned percent (4) and right-aligned reset (6) with one space between columns - so the percent and the countdown share one axis and the bar starts and ends on the same columns on every row. The longest line stays within the sidebar width and never wraps.
- The `◈ OPENCODE GO` header no longer draws by default; the panel is three lines unless `header: true` opts it back in.
- `sidebar.footer.go` accepts `true`/`false` or a look object (`header`, `barWidth`, `labelWidth`, `percent`, `reset`, `sweep`, each falling back to its default). `true` keeps the default look (no header, 14-cell bar, 6-wide labels, both columns, static meter). The meter is static by default and changes only when the percentage itself changes; `sweep: true` opts the travelling highlight back in.

## [0.14.0] - 2026-10-11

### Changed

- The `go` row and the footer Go panel now resolve the Zen Go key from OpenCode's own credential store. The pinned `@opencode/plugin` client declares `credential.list()`, so the bridge calls it directly on every poll and uses the `key`-type entry for the `opencode-go` integration, preferring the `active` one. `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` becomes an optional fallback, read only when the store holds no usable entry. A host whose client predates `credential.list`, a rejected call, or a malformed payload degrades to the env var and then to the row's "no key" dash without making a request. The key is never logged and never leaves the Authorization header.

## [0.13.0] - 2026-10-11

### Added

- A live Go usage panel in the sidebar footer slot, enabled with `sidebar.footer.go`. It draws three lines - `Rolling` (`5h`), `Weekly` (`1w`), `Monthly` (`1m`) - each with a ten-cell bar, a whole-number percent and a reset countdown, using the `context` row's bar glyphs and the `go` row's error tone (90% or more, or a non-`ok` window status). It is off by default, claims the footer slot even when `sidebar.footer.lines` is empty, and shares the `go` row's single account-wide poll of `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` rather than starting a second one. With no data yet it draws three dim resting lines, never a blank slot.

## [0.12.0] - 2026-10-09

### Changed

- The `tps` numerator now counts generation tokens - output plus reasoning - over the same streaming-span union, so a thinking-heavy turn reads as speed instead of idle time with no output yet. Tool settlement is still excluded, the denominator still ends at `streamed`, and the `reasoning` row itself is unchanged.

## [0.11.0] - 2026-10-08

### Changed

- TPS now reports a delta-based instantaneous rate instead of the session-lifetime average. The display is an integer, smoothed with an EWMA, with hysteresis so the last digit does not flicker, a minimum token sample before the rate is trusted, and an idle freeze that holds the last value when no new tokens arrive.
- The `context` row now reads as an estimate (`~`), reflecting that the underlying usage figure is approximate.
- The cache hit-rate denominator is now documented as deliberate in code and docs.

### Fixed

- `treeTotals` now wraps each per-id lookup in its own `try/catch`, so one bad id no longer blanks the cost/total rollup.
- Width-aware clipping keeps rows inside the rail instead of overflowing it.
- Per-session maps are now LRU-capped, closing a slow leak across long sessions.
- The `ses` row documents that the display is a pruned preview while click-to-copy still copies the full id.

## [0.10.4] - 2026-10-06

### Fixed

- The default `caution.exemptTools` list now carries the `tools.`-prefixed aliases (`tools.delegate`, `tools.delegate_many`, `tools.subagent`, `tools.task`) alongside the bare names it already exempted. Matching is by exact name, and the host reaches these delegated-work tools under both spellings, so a fresh install lit the row on ordinary delegation the bare names were meant to cover. The schema default and `flight-deck.example.jsonc` carry the same eleven names.
- The `caution` rail row draws a single-cell severity mark (`●` caution, `▲` watch) instead of `:warning:`. The bundled `string-width` tests emoji-regex before East-Asian width and charges `⚠` two cells — and Windows Terminal draws it that way — so the annunciator ran a column wider than every other row. Severity now rides a coloured run on the mark itself (`error` for a caution, `warning` for a watch) while the words keep the row's colour, and a test measures the drawn row in cells at the rail's real width.

## [0.10.3] - 2026-10-02

### Changed

- The `ses` row no longer bleeds past the rail. It again draws a short-pruned preview of the session id - width-aware, with an ellipsis, so it reads as a preview of a longer value - instead of the full 30-character id wrapping out of bounds. The click still copies the **full** id; only the display is pruned.
- A successful copy is now silent. The success toast is gone, since the copied value is already on the clipboard when the gesture works. A copy that could **not** be confirmed still shows its failure toast - a silent no-op must never masquerade as a success.

# Install - oc-flight-deck

Compatible with opencode 2.1.1 or newer (2.x).

One route: the npm registry. Plugin entries are bare strings in the `plugins` array of `opencode.jsonc`.

```jsonc
{ "plugins": ["oc-flight-deck"] }
```

Use the package name (`"oc-flight-deck"`): it resolves through npm and honours the package's `exports`. A local directory path will not work — OpenCode looks for `index.js`/`index.ts` at the directory root, ignores `exports`, and drops the entry silently (no load, no error, no log line). This is a real limitation, not a supported route.

The bare name tracks the newest release; append `@<version>` to pin an exact published version. The npm tarball ships the compiled `dist/` (the `prepublishOnly` step builds it before packing), so the registry entry always has a working entry point. Restart OpenCode after editing the config.

The TUI half has no direct observation surface in this build; verify it by its visible effect (the sidebar rendering).

oc-flight-deck guide

## How it works The plugin registers one sidebar rail and one ticker. On every tick it reads what the host already recorded and redraws the rows that changed; it never writes to the session and never blocks a turn. **Three scopes decide which numbers you see.** `cost`, `tokens`, `cache`, `reasoning` and `tps` roll up the open conversation plus the subagent sessions the host links to it by `parentID`. `project` covers every session in the project. `elapsed` counts active turn time, not wall clock. The link is the host's own: an independently spawned top-level session is not counted as a child, and `project` is the surface for that. **Refresh behaviour.** The rail ticks every `refresh` milliseconds (default `100`, allowed range 0–60000; values 1–15 clamp up to 16). While nothing is happening the tick backs off to about one second, so an idle session costs almost nothing. `refresh: 0` turns the ticker off entirely: clock-derived rows then move only when the host fires an event, and a row that needs a tick to change its number simply stops moving. Host events always redraw immediately, whatever the interval. **Restart safety.** Elapsed time and speed are recomputed from the assistant-turn spans the host recorded, not accumulated in memory, so a restart does not reset the clock and elapsed time never steps backwards while the host still reports those turns. **Config precedence.** Host plugin options beat `flight-deck.jsonc`, which beats the defaults, merged key by key. A bad value restores its default and raises a one-time toast naming the key. ## Panels ### Codex account limits Add `"dex"` to `sidebar.rows` in `flight-deck.jsonc` to show the Codex CLI account's 5h and 1w usage, in that order. It uses the Go row's compact dials, spacing and error/reset indicators, under its own `dex` label. These are Codex/ChatGPT plan limits, not OpenCode Go usage or the selected OpenCode model's allowance. The account is the one authenticated in Codex. Requires an authenticated native Codex CLI. On Windows, Flight Deck starts a private `codex app-server --stdio` inside an owned Job Object. It does not start a shared daemon or change privileges. On other platforms, a running authenticated daemon with `app-server proxy` support is required; start it separately with `codex app-server daemon start`. Flight Deck never starts or stops that shared daemon. No new account, paid service or API key is required beyond your existing Codex/ChatGPT plan. Codex manages its own authentication. The plugin polls once per minute through a short-lived private connection. It reads only account metadata and rate limits, never OAuth files or thread history. On Windows, the native server is created suspended, assigned to a kill-on-close job, then resumed. A hidden built-in PowerShell helper holds the job and the owner's process identity handle. Success closes stdin; timeout or cancellation terminates only that helper. Helper exit/crash or owner death closes the job and reaps all server descendants, including detached children. Scoop shims are bypassed so the native server, not a launcher, is contained before it can run. Missing daemon, API-key authentication, invalid windows, expired resets and data older than 90 seconds show unavailable rather than fabricated zero usage. One rail, in the order you list the rows, dimmed under any fixed lines. A session with subagents, defaults, a 200k window: ```text status ⠙ running agent build model claude-sonnet-4-5 · high cost $1.84 · 3 subagents project $12.40 · 21 sessions tokens 1.2M in · 84k out cache 92% hit · 1.1M read context ████████░░ ~78% perms 1 waiting · bash elapsed 2h 14m 07s tps 41 tok/s ``` Which rows draw is `sidebar.rows`; what each row's number means is the Rows table under Configure it. **The footer.** `sidebar.footer.lines` puts fixed text in the host footer slot, outside the rail cap; the documented branding pair is `["▸ FLIGHT DECK","─────────────────"]`. **The Go panel.** `sidebar.footer.go` adds the live Go usage panel: three fixed-width lines above the host location row, sharing one account-wide poll with the `go` row. ## Configure it One global file: `~/.config/opencode/flight-deck.jsonc`. The `.json` name is also read, and `.jsonc` is tried first. When `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` holds an absolute path, the file lives at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/flight-deck.jsonc` instead. There is no per-project lookup, so a copy left in a project root configures nothing. A missing file is normal and silent: you get the defaults. Comments and trailing commas are accepted by the Bun-hosted TUI. ```jsonc { "sidebar": { "rows": ["status", "cost", "context", "elapsed"] } } ``` ### Settings **Refresh** | Key | Default | Effect | | --- | --- | --- | | **`refresh`** | `100` | Milliseconds between ticks, 0–60000. Values 1–15 clamp to 16; `0` turns the ticker off, so clock-derived rows move only on host events. While idle the tick backs off to about 1s. | **Sidebar** | Key | Default | Effect | | --- | --- | --- | | **`lifetimeTotalsPath`** | `~/.local/share/opencode/flight-deck/totals.json` | Optional file for the lifetime total's high-water mark. Realtime speed plus time to first token: ```jsonc { "sidebar": { "rows": ["status", "tps", "elapsed"], "tps": { "display": "both" } } } ``` Silence every toast with one key: ```jsonc { "notifications": { "enabled": false } } ``` Watchdog on for long runs: ```jsonc { "sidebar": { "rows": ["status", "caution", "cost", "elapsed"] }, "caution": { "enabled": true } } ``` ## Commands The plugin exposes no tools and no CLI: it draws, and the host owns the session. The read-only host commands below are how you check it, and how you find the file this guide names. | Command | What it returns | | --- | --- | | `opencode plugin check` | Whether every configured plugin loads. Run it first when the rail does not draw. | | `opencode plugin list` | The loaded plugins, including `oc-flight-deck`. | | `opencode debug paths` | The config root that holds `flight-deck.jsonc`. | The shipped `flight-deck.example.jsonc` is a complete starting file, and `flight-deck.schema.json` validates your own against every key above. ## Troubleshooting **The rail does not draw.** Run `opencode plugin check`, confirm `oc-flight-deck` is in the loaded list, then restart. A rail with `sidebar.enabled: false` is loaded but invisible by design. **A row is missing.** Only rows named in `sidebar.rows` draw, and the default list is 11 of them; add the rest by name. Unknown names are ignored with a one-time warning. With `persist: false`, a row with no data yet is omitted rather than drawn as a zero. **A number looks wrong after a restart.** Cost, tokens, and context come from what the host recorded; elapsed and speed are recomputed from turn spans. If the host did not record the turns — a session restored from elsewhere — those rows start from what exists rather than inventing the gap. **`cost` and `project` disagree.** They answer different questions. `cost` is this conversation plus its subagent tree; `project` is every session in the project, including sessions that were never children of this one. **The `context` gauge is not exact.** It is an occupancy proxy, drawn with a `~` on purpose. It is not the model's own token count. **A config value is ignored.** A bad value restores its default and toasts once naming the key; silence that toast with `notifications.config: false`. A file in a project root configures nothing — the only file read is the global one. **The `go` row is blank.** It reads OpenCode's active opencode-go credential store. With no such credential there is nothing to read, and no environment variable sets it. **Toasts are noisy.** `notifications.enabled: false` silences every kind at once. The four flags under it only ever silence. ## Limitations - The context gauge is an estimate derived from recorded request sizes, not a measurement from the model. - Cache hit rate excludes cache writes from the denominator by design; a figure that includes them would be a different metric, not a more accurate one. - `cost` follows the host's `parentID` link only. Work done in an unrelated top-level session shows in `project` and nowhere else. - `branch` costs a VCS call per read, which is why it is off by default. - `guard` has no data unless a guard bridge supplies it. - `go` depends on an active opencode-go credential; it cannot report quota for any other provider. - The caution annunciator only reports. It never aborts, kills, retries, or blocks a turn. - One global config file, no per-project override: a per-repo look is a non-feature here. - No tools are registered, so nothing in this package is callable by an agent. ## Links - Source: - Package: - Issues: - OpenCode V2 plugin API: - Example config: [flight-deck.example.jsonc](../flight-deck.example.jsonc) - Config schema: [flight-deck.schema.json](../flight-deck.schema.json) - Install: [INSTALL.md](../INSTALL.md) - Changelog: [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md) - Releases: - Licence: MIT, see [LICENSE](../LICENSE)
